aliases.name: Goatman
aliases.meaning: Colloquial name for the part-man, part-goat figure

description.summary: An urban-legend cryptid said to inhabit the Norfolk Southern railway trestle over Pope Lick Creek in the Fisherville neighborhood of Louisville, Kentucky. Described as a part-man, part-goat (and sometimes part-sheep) creature that lures trespassers onto the active trestle.
description.full: The Pope Lick Monster is a Louisville, Kentucky urban legend centered on the Norfolk Southern Railway trestle that crosses Pope Lick Creek in the Fisherville neighborhood east of the city. Witnesses and storytellers describe a creature that is part-man and part-goat (sometimes also described as part-sheep), with a human-like body, fur-covered legs, cloven hooves, horns, and a deformed humanoid face. Variant accounts attribute to it the ability to mimic human voices, a hypnotic or siren-like lure, and in more lurid retellings a bloodied axe with which it chases trespassers. The legend's mortal danger is the trestle itself: 90 feet tall, 772 feet long, and carrying active freight rail. Multiple deaths and serious injuries since the 1980s have been associated with people climbing the trestle in connection with the legend, including 17-year-old Jack 'J.C.' Bahm II in 1988, 26-year-old Roquel Bain in April 2016, and 15-year-old Savanna Bright in May 2019. The legend was popularized by filmmaker Ron Schildknecht's 1988 short film 'The Legend of the Pope Lick Monster' and has appeared in regional television features and documentaries on cryptids.

etymology.origin: Named for Pope Lick Creek, the small tributary of Floyds Fork beneath the railroad trestle in eastern Jefferson County, Kentucky. 'Pope Lick' itself derives from a salt lick on land owned by the Pope family in early Kentucky settlement.
etymology.meaning: 'Pope Lick Monster' simply localizes the legend to its trestle; 'Goatman' refers to the satyr-like body plan
etymology.first_use: The legend's modern form was widely popularized after Ron Schildknecht's 1988 short film 'The Legend of the Pope Lick Monster'

origins.cultural_roots: The legend is a 20th-century American urban legend, layered onto an older folk landscape of trestle dares, 'goatman' figures, and rural Kentucky storytelling.
origins.earliest_accounts: Oral tradition in Louisville from at least the late 20th century; first widely documented in the 1988 short film by Ron Schildknecht.
origins.folklore_connections: Connected to the wider American 'goatman' urban-legend complex (e.g. Maryland's Goatman, Lake Worth Monster) and ultimately to satyr motifs from classical mythology.

history.modern_era: The Pope Lick Monster legend persists as a high-profile example of an urban legend with real-world consequences. Norfolk Southern, Louisville Metro Government, and the Parklands of Floyds Fork have repeatedly warned the public against trespass on the trestle, and victims' families have campaigned for additional fencing and warning signage. The legend is regularly revisited in regional news features and US cryptid documentaries.

notable.name: Death of Jack 'J.C.' Bahm II on the trestle

location.description: Pope Lick Trestle, Fisherville, Louisville, Kentucky

notable.description: 17-year-old Jack 'J.C.' Charles Bahm II was struck and killed by a train while on the Pope Lick trestle; a companion was injured. Local news coverage and later retrospectives connected the incident to the Pope Lick Monster legend.

credibility.notes: Treated as a real-world tragedy connected to legend-tripping rather than as a paranormal sighting.

notable.name: Death of Roquel Bain on the trestle

location.description: Pope Lick Trestle, Fisherville, Louisville, Kentucky

notable.description: 26-year-old Ohio tourist Roquel Bain was struck and killed by a train while on the trestle, having traveled to Louisville specifically to look for the Pope Lick Monster. Her boyfriend survived by hanging from the trestle's edge.

credibility.notes: The most widely reported real-world incident tied to the legend.

notable.name: Death of Savanna Bright on the trestle

location.description: Pope Lick Trestle, Fisherville, Louisville, Kentucky

notable.description: 15-year-old Savanna Bright was killed on the trestle; her companion Kaylee Keeling survived with serious injuries. The incident reignited family-led advocacy for stronger fencing and signage at the trestle.

credibility.notes: Most recent widely reported fatality linked to legend-tripping at the site.

skeptical.name: Pure urban legend / legend-tripping
skeptical.description: The Pope Lick Monster is a contemporary urban legend whose only physical effect is the dangerous behavior it inspires; the trestle is the real hazard, not a cryptid.
